title: Single and Multiple Separate LSTM Neural Networks for Multiple Output Feature Purchase Prediction
authors: Ciric, M.; Predic, B.; Stojanovic, D.; Ciric, I.
tldr: Compares single multivariate LSTM versus multiple separate LSTM networks for predicting next purchase timing and product category from medical vendor transaction data.
problem_and_motivation: Predicting both the timing and product category of a customer's next purchase is challenging because these outputs require different modeling approaches and may benefit from shared or separate representations.
approach: Uses transaction data from a medical drugs and devices vendor with GPI classification for product categories.
Transforms original purchase transactions into time series of input features for next purchase prediction.
Compares single multivariate LSTM (SMLSTM) against multi-network configurations (MLSTM + PMLSTM) for simultaneous category and day prediction.
Evaluates across three dataset sizes: 100+ purchases, 20+ purchases, and 5+ purchases.
Measures prediction accuracy for drug group/category vectors and next purchase day.
findings: num: For drug category prediction, dedicated LSTMs (MLSTM) significantly outperform single multivariate LSTM (SMLSTM).
num: For next purchase day prediction, single multivariate LSTM (SMLSTM) generally outperforms dedicated LSTMs.
num: For 95.7% of customers, at least one purchased drug category was correctly predicted.
num: At least four categories correctly predicted for 51.19% of customers.
num: No more than one category incorrectly predicted for 81.17% of customers.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: This paper provides a systematic comparison of single multivariate LSTM versus multiple dedicated LSTM networks for purchase prediction. It demonstrates that dedicated networks perform better for category prediction while shared networks perform better for timing prediction. The data transformation approach from transaction format to time series enables personalized marketing systems based on next-purchase forecasting.
directly_justifies: Dedicated LSTMs outperform single LSTM for drug category prediction.
Single multivariate LSTM outperforms dedicated LSTMs for next purchase day prediction.
95.7% of customers have at least one correct category prediction.
limits: Medical vendor data limits generalizability to general retail or personal finance.
No comparison with non-LSTM architectures like Transformers.
Data transformation process requires proprietary GPI classification system.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 topic domains was conducted. Topics 6.A (Predictive Modeling) and 6.B (Forecasting Algorithms) were rated high for the LSTM purchase prediction models. Topic 3.A (Expense Categorization) was rated medium for the GPI classification system. Topics 1.x-2.x, 4.x-5.x, 7.x-14.x were rejected as the paper focuses on algorithmic purchase prediction from transaction data, not personal finance demographics, system design, or budgeting.

limitations: Medical vendor data may not generalize to consumer retail or personal finance.
No comparison with Transformer or attention-based architectures.
Limited evaluation metrics; no precision/recall for timing prediction accuracy.
